rules.rationale: Halides showed the most negative source refractive-index effect; Moss relation inverts low polarizability into wide band gaps.
Chalcogenides raised source refractive index; polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise valence band and shrink the gap.
Largest source effect on refractive index; covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors under the Moss inversion.
High mean-Z boosted source refractive index; diffuse heavy-atom orbitals increase bandwidth and reduce band gap.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the dielectric source effects with reversed sign via the Moss/Ravindra inverse index-gap relation. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist, e.g. ionic heavy oxides, or where source field confidence is too low to invert reliably.

rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder.
Partially filled d bands introduce states near the Fermi level, narrowing or closing gaps; source evidence here was near-zero confidence.
Pnictides are weakly ionic covalent semiconductors; small electronegativity difference yields small experimental gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity difference and downweights the near-zero-confidence transition-metal source relation. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and heavily distorted or defect-dominated experimental structures where measured gaps deviate from ionicity ordering.

fixed_initial.lesson: The source study optimized refractive index, an objective inversely coupled to band gap through the Moss relation, and its per-field confidences are low (0.006-0.30). Direct transfer would push search toward narrow-gap chalcogenides and metalloids, exactly the wrong direction. Domain ionicity chemistry supplies the same ordering with independent mechanistic support, so it is the safer frozen deployment while the inverted-transfer skill remains the diagnostic alternative.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Rebuilt the output to satisfy the schema: exactly two skills with distinct descriptive IDs, every conditions object mapping a real catalog field directly to an exact catalog value (anion_family, dominant_family, mean_atomic_number_bin, transition_metal_flag), no placeholder keys or numeric suffixes, all parameters inside allowed ranges, one two-condition interaction used only where mechanistically justified, rationales under 25 words and hypotheses under 45 words, plus selected_skill_id, lesson, and revision_summary. Source transfer evidence was used unchanged and no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are referenced.

rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in the gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Domain proposal ordering candidates by cation-anion electronegativity difference: reward ionic halides and oxides, penalize polarizable chalcogenides, mildly penalize d-band metals. Fails for d0/d10 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated measurements.

rules.rationale: Halides carried the most negative source refractive-index effect; low polarizability inverts to wide gaps through the Moss relation.
Reverses the lowest-confidence source relation: d0/d10 transition-metal oxides are classic wide-gap ionic insulators, not narrow-gap metals.
Chalcogen-dominated compositions raised source refractive index; polarizable p-states imply small experimental gaps under Moss inversion.
Very heavy mean-Z increased source index; diffuse relativistic orbitals broaden bands and reduce measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Source-grounded counter-hypothesis: invert dielectric effects (halide, chalcogen, heavy-Z) while reversing the near-zero-confidence transition-metal penalty toward wide-gap d0 oxides. Fails if index and gap co-vary positively or if inversion misreads weak source signals.

true_feedback.lesson: Across two independent development generations the ionicity ladder led on mean AUC (72.7 vs 65.3, then 81.3 vs 73.5) with comparable final-best, so domain electronegativity ordering remains the safer frozen choice given source per-field confidences of only 0.006-0.30. Weak seeds appeared for both skills, indicating task variance rather than a specific rule defect, so I only softened the broad transition-metal penalty that conflicts with wide-gap d0 oxides instead of restructuring the skill.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Deployed skill v3 keeps the winning ionicity ladder, slightly strengthens the closed-shell halide interaction, deepens the chalcogenide penalty, and reduces the blanket transition-metal penalty from -0.30 to -0.22 because d0 oxides are wide-gap counterexamples; semantic mass end was trimmed to hand more late mass to the target-only anchor. The alternative is rebuilt as a sharper counter-hypothesis that keeps Moss-inverted source evidence (halide, chalcogen-dominant, very-high mean-Z) but explicitly reverses the lowest-confidence transition-metal relation via a d0-oxide interaction and switches the polarizability penalty from anion_family to the dominant_family chalcogen axis for diversity. All conditions map catalog fields to exact catalog values, each skill uses four rules, and all parameters lie inside the allowed ranges; feedback informed only relative ranking, not causal claims.

rules.rationale: Chalcogenides gave the largest positive source index effect; polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band and shrink gaps under Moss inversion.
Metalloids produced the strongest source effect (9.23); covalent metalloid networks are textbook narrow-gap semiconductors, so the inverted sign is strongly negative.
Halides gave the most negative source index effect; low anion polarizability inverts via Moss into wide experimental gaps, a source-grounded positive rule.
Mean-Z-high was a top source index driver (6.07); diffuse heavy-atom orbitals broaden bands, so the inverted gap penalty is retained.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the sign of the four highest-effect source fields through the Moss index-gap inversion. It should fail where source confidence is lowest, and for heavy ionic oxides where high index and wide gap coexist.

rules.rationale: Main-group halides combine maximal electronegativity contrast with closed-shell cations and no d-states in the gap, the widest-gap configuration.
Deep O 2p valence bands plus strong ionicity place oxides high on the cation-anion electronegativity-contrast ladder.
Pnictides are weakly ionic covalent semiconductors; small electronegativity contrast and dispersive bands keep measured gaps modest.
Reverses the near-zero-confidence transition-metal source relation: localized 4f and d-derived states near the Fermi level tend to narrow measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Orders families by cation-anion electronegativity contrast and downweights the lowest-confidence source relation (lanthanide, 0.006) instead of reversing it. Fails for d0 and f0 wide-gap oxides and for defect-dominated measurements that break ionicity ordering.

no_feedback.lesson: The source task maximized refractive index, which couples inversely to gap through the Moss relation, but its per-field confidences are low (0.006-0.30) and the metalloid and mean-Z effects are the only high-confidence ones. A flat sign reversal therefore risks over-rotating the search toward covalent chalcogenides. Ionicity-contrast chemistry reproduces the expected wide-gap ordering from independent physics, while the lanthanide rule tests the least-confident source relation without assuming its sign, making it the safer frozen deployment choice.
no_feedback.revision_summary: No measured development feedback was available, so both skills were re-derived from the original source effects and catalog values only. The inverted-transfer skill keeps the Moss logic but drops the weak light-nonmetal and alkaline-earth source signals and trims to the four highest-confidence relations. The domain skill replaces the reversed transition-metal term with a lanthanide downweight, which targets the single lowest-confidence source relation directly, and keeps one chemically meaningful halide/main-group interaction. All conditions use exact catalog field-value pairs, all parameters sit inside allowed ranges, and no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are referenced.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across two independent eight-seed development batches the Moss-inverted transfer skill led on mean AUC (72.7 then 74.9) while the ionicity ladder trailed (65.3 then 72.6), and each skill collapsed on different single seeds, so instability is seed-specific rather than skill-specific. Two separate batches favoring the same skill is weaker evidence than a controlled study but stronger than one batch, so the source-grounded inversion is frozen and the ionicity ladder is retained as the mechanistic counter-hypothesis.
